draft.title: Mind and body questions
card: Philosophers have long asked how the mind relates to the body. The mind means thoughts, feelings and awareness. The body includes the brain.
the view that the mind and body are two separate things. On this view, the mind is not made of physical matter.
the view that the mind and body are one thing. On this view, mental life is part of the physical body.
Modern psychology studies mental processes through the brain, which treats them as linked to the body. Researchers measure brain activity and link it to thoughts and behaviour.
draft.remember: Dualism splits mind from body. Monism joins them, and modern psychology studies the mind through the brain.

a.q: Which view says that the mind and body are separate things?
a.why: Dualism means two: the mind and body are separate. Monism is the opposite view, that they are one thing. Phrenology and neuroimaging are not views about the mind and body.
a.clue: Think of the prefix: du- means two.

b.q: Dr Lee studies how memory works by scanning which brain areas are active as people recall words. Which view does her approach fit best?
opts: Mental processes can be studied through the brain
The mind is separate and cannot be linked to the body
Thoughts have no connection to any physical process
The body can only be studied apart from the mind
b.why: Linking memory to brain activity treats mental processes as tied to the body, which fits the modern approach and the monist view. The tempting option, that the mind is separate, describes dualism, which would not expect brain scans to explain mental life.
b.clue: Which option links thinking to something that can be measured in the body?

b.best: Mental processes can be studied through the brain
